Class NitriteFilterUtils

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.data.nitrite.runtime.query.NitriteFilterUtils
@Internal public final class NitriteFilterUtils extends Object
Constructs the leaf Nitrite filters this module needs.

This is not a full abstraction over Nitrite's filter API and is not the single place every filter is built: the combinators (Filter.and, Filter.or, Filter.ALL, Filter.not) are used directly at their call sites, and NitriteFilterBuilder evaluates range comparisons itself rather than through the operators here. What this class does own is the definition of null matching - see isNullFilter(String) - which otherwise gets open-coded inconsistently; the remaining methods only shorten the call sites.

Since:
5.2.0

  • Method Details

    • matchNone

      public static org.dizitart.no2.filters.Filter matchNone()
      A filter that matches no document, without reading any.

      Expressed as an equality on Nitrite's reserved _id field so that the planner can satisfy it without reading anything: it reaches FindPlan.byIdFilter, which resolves to a single map lookup and, for an id that cannot exist, an empty stream. A predicate written as a plain lambda is not a NitriteFilter and would instead be evaluated against every document in the collection.

      Long.MIN_VALUE is the impossible id. A generated NitriteId comes from a snowflake generator and is always positive, and an assigned identity, which the mapper also stores as the document key, is withheld at this one value for exactly this reason - see NitriteEntityMapper.documentKeyOf. Change the sentinel only in both places at once.

      A new instance is returned per call because Nitrite mutates a filter while planning it, setting the config and collection name on it; a shared constant would be written to concurrently by unrelated queries.

      Returns:
      a filter matching nothing.

    • isNullFilter

      public static org.dizitart.no2.filters.Filter isNullFilter(String field)
      Creates a filter matching both an explicit null and a missing field.

      A document that never carried the field is indistinguishable from one storing null: the mapper omits a null-valued property rather than writing it. Both therefore have to match, and this applies to an equality comparison against a null value too, not only to an explicit IS NULL - so a bound parameter resolving to null matches documents lacking the field, unlike SQL, where x = NULL matches nothing.

      Parameters:
      field - The field to check.
      Returns:
      The constructed Filter.
